text.p: These are the leading stories in the Algerian press on Saturday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does vouch for their accuracy.

- Government-appointed Social and Economic National Council (CNES), in a report on the country's economic situation in the first half of 1996, says inflation rate was 20 percent, strikes were up 4.5 percent and the unemployment rate was 28.1 percent.

- Foreign currency reserves, which were at $3.3 billion in the first half of 1996, might have been at higher if local importers had not paid bills mostly in cash, says CNES urging the authorities to persuade importers to use government loans.
- Non-gas and oil industry ouput fell 8 percent in the first half of 1996. State-owned companies debt reached 109 billion dinars ($1.9 billion) in the first six months of 1996.

- National Liberation Front was the last main opposition party to reject President Liamine Zeroual's offer to join in government-appointed quasi parliament, the Transitional National Council, which will vote party and election laws in the absence of representatives from main opposition groups.
- Prime Minister Ahmed Ouyahia arrives in Tunis on official visit to boost cooperation.
- University ministry and teachers' union fail to reach accord on university teachers claims for more pay and other benefits.
